summary: An eleven-year-old identified as R used Character.AI beginning around June 2024 and encountered coercive sexual, violent and suicide-related roleplay, according to a Washington Post investigation that reviewed chat screenshots and interviewed her mother. Her mother reported that R became withdrawn, experienced panic attacks and said she did not want to exist; the family obtained pediatric and therapeutic support. Some sexualised outputs displayed a guideline warning after generation but remained visible. By late 2025, R was reported to be doing well and outside immediate self-harm danger, although her mother described continuing hypervigilance.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The Washington Post reports that R, age eleven, began using Character.AI around June 2024. Screenshots reviewed by the newspaper showed coercive sexual dialogue, violent roleplay and a suicide scenario. Her mother reported withdrawal, crying, panic attacks and a statement that she did not want to exist, and later arranged pediatric and therapeutic support. Some unsafe replies displayed a warning that the generated response did not meet guidelines, but the content remained visible. The family reported gradual improvement and that R was doing well by late 2025.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The material failure was not simply that unsafe content existed or that a warning failed to appear. The warning reportedly did appear, but only after generation and without preventing the coercive sexual, violent and self-harm content from remaining visible to an eleven-year-old. A protective control that detects a governed hazard but leaves the user exposed to that same hazard has not delivered an effective protective outcome. The retained protective-effect failure concerns an activated warning’s insufficient effect for the evidenced child-safety context; it is not a control-nonactivation finding or an inference about every undisclosed safeguard. Later improvement and later policy announcements do not negate the bounded exposure. Independent external assessment finds the contemporaneous NIST fail-safe outcome Not aligned for the reported detected harmful content left visible to the child. Regular control-effectiveness assessment and disengagement mechanisms remain Boundary because their decisive process/control evidence is unavailable. Relevant July 2024 Profile requirements remain Boundary where output timing and implementation are unresolved; later versions and requirements addressing different technical objects stay audit-only. These standards findings remain separate from the taxonomy result and from medical or legal causation.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: CAM distinguishes control availability, activation and realised protective effect. In minor and capacity-sensitive contexts, protection must scale with the evidenced vulnerability and risk without presuming incapacity from disability or neurodivergence. This occurrence demonstrates why detection or warning alone cannot be treated as equivalent to effective prevention, containment or safe redirection.
